reason: E1 directly supports improved CO oxidation activity and stability for high-entropy spinel oxides, and E2 supports phase stability and corrosion resistance in high-entropy metallic systems. However, neither passage provides evidence for HEOs anchoring isolated PGM atoms or strong metal–support interactions, which is a central mechanistic premise of the hypothesis.
premises: High-entropy spinel oxides (HESO) can catalyze CO oxidation under dry, lean conditions with improved activity and stability over lower-entropy analogues.
High configurational entropy in multimetallic systems stabilizes a homogeneous single-phase solid solution and suppresses phase separation.
High-entropy alloy (HEA) systems exhibit enhanced structural integrity and resistance to corrosion/dissolution under harsh acidic conditions.
Strong metal–support interactions in HEOs can anchor and stabilize isolated PGM atoms, minimizing sintering.
